selected_leaf.scope: One bounded in-Chat finite model comparing path-only, repository numeric-id-only, node_id-only, and repository-local monotonic-generation claims under stale claimant, repository lifecycle identity change, response-loss retry, CAS conflict, and rate-limit interruption. Authority-object rollback/delete-recreate is deliberately excluded and retained as the next unresolved child.
selected_leaf.execution_mode: Explicit finite case table reasoned in scheduled Chat; no Python, hosted runner, Codespaces, external model/API compute, protected-primary execution, or manual-user execution.
common_protocol_assumptions: Any accepted effect must be preceded by an authority decision; transport/read/write uncertainty fails closed.
Repository content mutation uses a current-blob SHA/CAS precondition and serial mutation discipline.
The monotonic-generation candidate stores generation plus stable transition_id; a response-loss retry is accepted as the same transition only when transition_id matches the committed record.

A repository lifecycle replacement is safe for the monotonic-generation candidate only when the authority record survives and is bumped before new-incarnation effects. Rollback/loss of that authority record is outside this slice and remains unresolved.

monotonic_generation.unresolved_outside_scope: authority-object rollback/delete-recreate can erase or rewind the monotonic witness

sources.use: Part118 narrowed official GitHub repository numeric id/node_id evidence: audited official pages exposed the identifiers but did not establish a permanent non-reuse guarantee across the full repository lifecycle.
GitHub repository-content mutation requires the current file SHA for updates; GitHub also documents conflicts for concurrent content mutations and recommends serial mutation.

GitHub documents 403/429 rate-limit responses and instructs clients not to retry until the indicated reset/retry-after boundary, supporting fail-closed checkpoint-and-next-invocation behavior rather than same-run retry.

observations: Static repository identity is not a generation witness. A stale claimant can retain the same path, numeric id, or node_id after a logical generation advance within the same repository identity.

Numeric id and node_id are useful as observed-change detectors when they actually differ, but Part118 did not establish permanent non-reuse semantics, so neither can close the incarnation proof by itself.
A monotonic generation plus stable transition_id and current-blob CAS resolves both stale-generation rejection and ambiguous response-loss retry within the tested persistent-authority scope.
Rate-limit interruption is a liveness event, not authority to guess. Safety requires no effect before a successful authority decision; continuation moves to a later invocation.
inferences: The highest-value generic claim shape is not path or repository identity alone but a monotonic incarnation/generation witness coupled to a stable transition identity and CAS authority update.

This is not yet an accepted zero-dependency coordination mechanism because the authority object is repository-local: if that object can be deleted, recreated, force-rewound, or restored together with the repository, the monotonic witness can regress.
scope_guard: No claim is made about arbitrary external sinks, permanent GitHub identifier non-reuse, cross-repository atomicity, or safety when the authority record itself is rolled back/lost. No O, other-role, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, scheduler, or protected-primary semantic input was used.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.reason_not_accepted: Authority-object rollback/delete-recreate remains an unresolved child; static GitHub repository identifiers also lack a proven permanent non-reuse guarantee in the audited scope.

unresolved_children: Authority-object rollback/delete-recreate: determine whether a repository-local monotonic generation can remain trustworthy when the authority file/repository itself is restored, force-rewound, deleted/recreated, or otherwise loses the latest witness without introducing an external hosted coordinator or finite quota dependency.
exact_continuation: Part120: execute one bounded role-local/public-source model of authority-object rollback/delete-recreate. Compare same-repository monotonic record, sibling-repository witness, commit-history/ancestor witness, and fail-closed unknown under force-rewind, delete/recreate, restore, stale claimant, and response-loss retry. Reject any route that needs external hosted coordination, richer-mode/manual execution, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, or incremental cost; persist one checkpoint and return with no second leaf.
